description.zh:
如何在 Java 中讀寫資料

每個程式最終都在處理資料，因此必須知道如何在程式中輸入與輸出。輸出使用 System.out.println(...)，可在括號中放入數字、字串或運算式：

System.out.println(5 + 10);
System.out.println(3 * 7);
System.out.println(2 * 2 * 2 * 2);  // 2 的 4 次方
System.out.println(37 / 3);   // 兩個 int 相除
System.out.println(37 % 3);   // 餘數

讀入資料使用 Scanner（需 import java.util.Scanner;）。nextLine() 讀取一整行文字：

Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
System.out.println("What is your name?");
String name = scanner.nextLine();
System.out.println("Hi " + name + "!");

範例輸入

John

輸出

What is your name?
Hi John!

數字相加 vs 字串連接

試著寫一個程式：讀入兩個數字並輸出它們的和。若用 nextLine() 讀入再相加：

String a = scanner.nextLine();
String b = scanner.nextLine();
String s = a + b;
System.out.println(s);

範例輸入

5
7

輸出

57

結果是 57 而不是 12！因為 + 在兩個 String 之間代表字串連接（把字串接在一起），不是數字相加。在學校裡我們學過 5 + 7 = 12，所以理解這個差異非常重要。

在 Java 中，每個值都有型別。例如 5 是 int（整數），"hello" 是 String（字串）。型別決定可以對它做哪些運算：兩個 int 可以相乘；兩個 String 不能用 * 相乘。

要把讀入的文字轉成整數，可用 Integer.parseInt(...)，或直接用 nextInt()：

int a = scanner.nextInt();
int b = scanner.nextInt();
int s = a + b;
System.out.println(s);

範例輸入

5
7

輸出

12

本章題目會反覆用到輸出、Scanner 讀取，以及整數與字串的差異。閱讀完畢後，點選下方「下一題」開始練習。
description.en:
How to read and write in Java

Every program is eventually a data processor, so we need to know how to input and output data. Use System.out.println(...) to print numbers, strings, or expressions:

System.out.println(5 + 10);
System.out.println(3 * 7);
System.out.println(2 * 2 * 2 * 2);  // 2 to the power of 4
System.out.println(37 / 3);   // int division
System.out.println(37 % 3);   // remainder

To read input, use Scanner (import java.util.Scanner;). nextLine() reads a full line of text:

Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
System.out.println("What is your name?");
String name = scanner.nextLine();
System.out.println("Hi " + name + "!");

Sample input

John

Output

What is your name?
Hi John!

Sum of numbers and strings

Try a program that reads two numbers and prints their sum. If you use nextLine() and add:

String a = scanner.nextLine();
String b = scanner.nextLine();
String s = a + b;
System.out.println(s);

Sample input

5
7

Output

57

The result is 57, not 12! With two String values, + means concatenation (gluing text together), not numeric addition. In school we learn 5 + 7 = 12—understanding this difference is essential.

In Java, every value has a type. For example, 5 is an int, and "hello" is a String. The type determines which operations are allowed: two int values can be multiplied; two String values cannot use *.

Convert text to integers with Integer.parseInt(...), or read integers directly with nextInt():

int a = scanner.nextInt();
int b = scanner.nextInt();
int s = a + b;
System.out.println(s);

Sample input

5
7

Output

12

Exercises in this chapter use output, Scanner, and the difference between integers and strings. When you are ready, click Next below.
